intent: Hold the iteration-6 geometry unchanged: five sensors at x = -0.06 to +0.06 in 0.03 m steps, y = 0.03, 16 mm footprints, wheel_track 0.10, wheel_radius 0.03, body_width 0.12, body_length 0.18, mass 0.8. This isolates the controller's kp reduction, as the Integrator requested. Expected result: slalom line loss falls from 0.35 toward 0.1 or below, oval progress recovers toward 0.5, and the score returns toward the 110 to 120 range. Max_error may stay near 0.063 m, which would show that the limit is gain balance rather than geometry. Considering, not committed: wheel_track back to 0.12 if line loss stays at 0.2 or higher or oval progress stays below 0.35; mass 0.7 with body_length 0.18 only if line loss is near 0.1 and max_error stays at about 0.063 m.
learning: Iteration 6 shows that narrowing wheel_track to 0.10 with the unchanged controller raised slalom line loss from 0.10 to 0.35 and halved oval progress, and did not move max_error below 0.06 m. So extra turn authority destabilised the line rather than fixing tracking. The open question is whether reducing kp on this platform brings line loss back under 0.2 without losing the tracking gain. If it does not, wheel_track 0.12 is the safer platform, and the remaining tracking error would be a controller limit rather than a geometry limit.
rationale: Iteration 6 (wheel_track 0.10, mass 0.8, body_length 0.18, sensor y 0.03, 16 mm footprints, 0.06 m span) scored 72.91, down from 111.80 in iteration 5. Slalom line loss rose from 0.10 to 0.35 per run, and oval progress fell from 0.55 to 0.28. Max_error did not improve: it was 0.0618 on oval, 0.0630 on s-bend and 0.0639 on slalom, still just above the 0.06 m off-track limit. The Integrator's stated rule applies: if slalom line loss is 0.2 or higher after this race, hold the geometry and reduce kp rather than change the array. I am taking that advice. Line loss is again the controllable failure, and the sensor span and forward offset are not the cause, so I am not changing them. I am also not reverting mass or body_length, because the inertia test (mass 0.7 with body_length 0.18) is only worth running once line loss is back near 0.1 with max_error still at about 0.063 m, and that condition is not met. I am keeping wheel_track at 0.10 so that the controller change is tested on the same platform. Iteration 6 also shows a cost of the narrower track: oval progress halved. If line loss stays at 0.2 or higher after the kp reduction, or oval progress stays below about 0.35, the next geometry step is to return wheel_track to 0.12 rather than try further inertia changes.
